summary: A Redmine-like MySQL query is slow because MySQL must evaluate a large issues-driven access path, correlated permission checks, and a non-sargable substring predicate while honoring ORDER BY issues.id DESC LIMIT 10. The reproduction should model the mechanism with sparse token hits concentrated in older/lower-id rows so the descending primary-key scan must walk a long distance before finding 10 matches.
symptoms: The reported query takes about 15 seconds in production.
EXPLAIN shows issues as the primary driving table with a large row estimate.
Dependent subqueries appear for enabled_modules and members.
The query filters on LOWER(issues.subject) LIKE LOWER('%255392%') and orders by issues.id DESC with LIMIT 10.
mechanism: MySQL scans issues by PRIMARY key in descending order to satisfy ORDER BY ... DESC LIMIT 10, but the token match is sparse and concentrated in low-id/old rows, so the scan must inspect many non-matching rows before enough qualifying rows are found. The join to projects and the permission subqueries remain post-filters, and LOWER(subject) LIKE '%255392%' is non-sargable, so the optimizer cannot use a subject index to jump directly to matching rows.

facts.evidence: The post says issues has more than 334,823 records.
The post says custom_values has over 1,350,243 records.
The post says projects has 494 records.
The post says the system currently has 1350 users.
The author says the slowest query takes about 15 seconds.
The post includes the full SELECT with an inner join to projects, EXISTS on enabled_modules, NOT IN on members, and a LOWER(subject) substring predicate.
The Tabular Explain in the post lists issues as PRIMARY with type range and rows 311632, projects as eq_ref, and dependent subqueries for members and enabled_modules.

value.effect: descending PK scan must inspect many rows before LIMIT 10 is satisfied

facts.evidence: The human feedback explicitly identifies sparse token placement on the issues.id DESC path as the key mechanism and asks to model token position distribution and effective hit rate.

assumptions: The slow query is dominated by the issues scan and post-filtering rather than by custom_values, which is mentioned in the post but not used in the shown SQL.
The partial schema and EXPLAIN are sufficient to recreate the optimizer shape even if the exact production schema differs.
issues.subject does not have an index that can make LIKE '%255392%' sargable in the reproduction.
Most projects have issue_tracking enabled so the EXISTS predicate remains visible but not highly selective.
The production incident may have additional statistics quirks that cannot be exactly reconstructed without a dump.
unknowns: Exact full schema and all indexes on issues and projects.
Whether the production data had histograms or stale statistics.
The exact distribution of subject values and visibility flags in production.
Whether session settings or application role affected the original plan.
